review_locator: PMCID:PMC10157204, New pairings and deorphanization among the atypical chemokine receptor family; PMCID:PMC10050359, Prospects for targeting ACKR1 in cancer and other diseases
primary_title: CXCL10 Is an Agonist of the CC Family Chemokine Scavenger Receptor ACKR2/D6
decision_basis: The reviews identify CXCL10 as a newly established ACKR2 ligand; the cited primary study shows beta-arrestin recruitment, specific binding, internalization and extracellular depletion of CXCL10 by ACKR2.
limitations_preserved: Record as atypical-receptor binding/scavenging with beta-arrestin-biased uptake; preserve unprocessed CXCL10 and DPP4/CD26 processing boundaries and do not infer canonical G-protein signaling or CNS/SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10157204, New pairings and deorphanization among the atypical chemokine receptor family; PMCID:PMC4901034, Atypical Chemokine Receptors and Their Roles in the Resolution of the Inflammatory Response
primary_title: CCL20 is a novel ligand for the scavenging atypical chemokine receptor 4
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL20 as a newly established ACKR4 ligand; the cited primary study shows fluorescent human and mouse CCL20 uptake by ACKR4 with species-dependent affinity and scavenging behavior.
limitations_preserved: Preserve lower affinity than CCL19/CCL21/CCL25, species-dependent uptake and noncanonical scavenging topology; no productive CCR6-equivalent signaling or CNS/SCI claim.

primary_title: Systematic reassessment of chemokine-receptor pairings confirms CCL20 but not CXCL13 and extends the spectrum of ACKR4 agonists to CCL22
decision_basis: The reviews report CCL22 as an additional ACKR4 ligand; the cited primary screening study identifies CCL22 as a potent partial agonist of human ACKR4 in beta-arrestin recruitment assays.
limitations_preserved: Record as partial agonism/scavenging-related ACKR4 activity rather than canonical G-protein signaling; preserve distinction from established CCR4/ACKR2 branches and no CNS/SCI claim.

primary_title: ACKR4 Recruits GRK3 Prior to beta-Arrestins but Can Scavenge Chemokines in the Absence of beta-Arrestins
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL25 as an ACKR4 ligand; the cited primary studies show CCL25-dependent beta-arrestin recruitment and ACKR4-mediated internalization/scavenging without Erk1/2, Akt or Src activation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve atypical scavenging and beta-arrestin/GRK3 context, with no canonical G-protein, Erk/Akt/Src relay or CNS/SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10157204, New pairings and deorphanization among the atypical chemokine receptor family; PMCID:PMC10050359, Prospects for targeting ACKR1 in cancer and other diseases
primary_title: GPR182 is an endothelium-specific atypical chemokine receptor that maintains hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis
decision_basis: The reviews identify GPR182 as an atypical receptor for CXCL10; the cited primary study shows CXCL10 binding to human and mouse GPR182, lack of G-protein/beta-arrestin signaling and in vivo chemokine regulation consistent with scavenging.
limitations_preserved: Preserve provisional ACKR5 nomenclature, low/relative affinity and non-signaling scavenger semantics; no canonical GPCR relay or CNS/SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10157204, New pairings and deorphanization among the atypical chemokine receptor family; PMCID:PMC6052832, The unique structural and functional features of CXCL12
primary_title: GPR182 is an endothelium-specific atypical chemokine receptor that maintains hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis
decision_basis: The reviews identify GPR182 as a second atypical receptor for CXCL12; the cited primary study shows fluorescent CXCL12 binding to GPR182, competition by CXCL10/CXCL12, absent classical signaling and altered circulating chemokine levels after endothelial Gpr182 loss.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CXCL12 isoform and GPR182/ACKR3/CXCR4 scavenger overlap, relative affinity and no canonical GPCR relay or CNS/SCI claim.

primary_title: GPR182 is an endothelium-specific atypical chemokine receptor that maintains hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis
decision_basis: The reviews identify GPR182 as an atypical receptor for CXCL13; the cited primary study shows CXCL13 binding to GPR182, absent classical signaling and chemokine regulation in vivo, supporting scavenger function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve GPR182 as provisional ACKR5 and distinguish scavenging from canonical CXCR5 signaling; no CNS/SCI claim.

primary_title: GPR182 is a broadly scavenging atypical chemokine receptor influencing T-independent immunity
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL28 as a newly validated GPR182 ligand; the cited primary study shows CCL28 binding and efficient scavenging by GPR182, with no canonical G-protein signaling and in vivo chemokine effects.
limitations_preserved: Preserve provisional ACKR5 nomenclature, scavenging-only/noncanonical signaling and CCL28-specific evidence; no canonical CCR10 relay or CNS/SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10157204, New pairings and deorphanization among the atypical chemokine receptor family; PMCID:PMC10050359, Prospects for targeting ACKR1 in cancer and other diseases
primary_title: Large chemokine binding spectrum of human and mouse atypical chemokine receptor GPR182 (ACKR5)
decision_basis: The reviews identify GPR182 as a broad atypical chemokine binding receptor; the cited primary profiling study detects human and mouse CXCL9 displacement/binding to GPR182 and associates GPR182 loss with chemokine accumulation.
limitations_preserved: Keep this as binding-only/low-affinity spectrum evidence; do not upgrade to direct scavenging kinetics, canonical GPCR signaling, or CNS/SCI function.
